chapter: Coming up in New York and Harlem theatres
title: Louis Prima and Keely Smith copying 'White Cliffs of Dover'
summary: Whaley says Louis Prima had his Apollo staging of 'White Cliffs of Dover' copied and published it as his own.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: You said you wanted to talk about Louis Prima.
You know, when Louis came into the Apollo, he had that -- his wife with him.

So we had -- Costin, she was a ingenue and we had White Cliffs of Dover and we had the girls singing against it, you know, like a kind of melody, they'd sing the kind of melody and she'd sing the melody and they would fill in with words, so Louis Prima got somebody to sit in the audience to copy all the words and he told all of his band to copy all of their part.

So after he had left the theatre about six weeks or so like that, he put out this song, White Cliffs of Dover, Louis Prima and I said, to the guy hey that's my number. He took that from the theatre. So I met him downtown one day and I said, hey, Louis, big number. Yeah. I said, well you give me something for that.
